sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vethantham.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Hi, how are you?
sentences.zh: 嗨，你好吗？

sentences.en: Oh, thank you.
sentences.zh: 哦，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Sarah and David Reza recently bought a place outside of Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 莎拉和戴维·雷扎最近在华盛顿特区外买了一处房产。

sentences.en: They sound excited because this is the first time they're hosting both their families.
sentences.zh: 他们听起来很兴奋，因为这是他们第一次同时招待双方的家人。

sentences.en: We are making today a vegetable frittata with tomato, basil, and goat cheese.
sentences.zh: 我们今天要做的是蔬菜烘蛋，配料有番茄、罗勒和山羊奶酪。

sentences.en: We've got home fries.
sentences.zh: 我们还准备了家常炸薯块。

sentences.en: Sarah and David wanted to start a new tradition.
sentences.zh: 莎拉和戴维想开启一项新传统。

sentences.en: Cook brunch with ingredients from their home garden.
sentences.zh: 用自家花园里的食材做早午餐。

sentences.en: The home fries have rosemary from our garden, and the frittata has basil from our garden.
sentences.zh: 家常炸薯块里用了我们花园里的迷迭香，烘蛋里用了我们花园里的罗勒。

sentences.en: This is Sarah's way of going back to her family's roots.
sentences.zh: 这是莎拉回归家庭根源的方式。

sentences.en: She remembers her mother doing the very same thing.
sentences.zh: 她记得她母亲也做过同样的事情。

sentences.en: I remember growing up, my mom had a garden, and she would always come back with these tiny little tomatoes
sentences.zh: 我记得小时候，我妈妈有个花园，她总是会带回这些小小的番茄，

sentences.en: and be like, I provided for my family.
sentences.zh: 然后说，我为家人提供了食物。

sentences.en: Look, family, I grew this.
sentences.zh: 看，家人们，这是我种的。

sentences.en: And we're like, yeah, that's the smallest tomato ever.
sentences.zh: 我们就会说，哇，这是有史以来最小的番茄。

sentences.en: But there's something about being able to grow stuff and being able to give it to people that you love
sentences.zh: 但能够种植东西并把它送给你爱的人，这种感觉很特别，

sentences.en: that's pretty exciting.
sentences.zh: 相当令人兴奋。

sentences.en: So, yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以，没错。

sentences.en: My grandmother would always say that, this is Sarah's brother, Zach.
sentences.zh: 我祖母总是会说，这是莎拉的兄弟，扎克。

sentences.en: The sharing food is important, but I'd say the most important part is being around the table.
sentences.zh: 分享食物很重要，但我认为最重要的是围坐在餐桌旁。

sentences.en: But food was the lure to get everyone done.
sentences.zh: 但食物是把大家聚在一起的诱饵。

sentences.en: Food, yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 食物，没错，正是如此。

sentences.en: Food kept us there.
sentences.zh: 食物让我们留在了那里。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Food brought us together, but it's the company in the conversation.
sentences.zh: 食物把我们聚在一起，但真正重要的是陪伴和交谈。

sentences.en: Today on Hidden Brain, the profound role that food plays in our lives.
sentences.zh: 今天在《隐藏的大脑》节目中，我们将探讨食物在我们生活中扮演的深远角色。

sentences.en: Food is not just nutrition that goes in your mouth or even pleasant sensations that go with it.
sentences.zh: 食物不仅仅是进入你口中的营养，甚至不仅仅是随之而来的愉悦感。

sentences.en: It connects to your whole life.
sentences.zh: 它与你的整个人生息息相关。

sentences.en: We look at the culture and psychology that determine what we eat, what we spit out, and when we come back for more.
sentences.zh: 我们研究决定我们吃什么、吐出什么以及何时再想吃什么的文化和心理。

sentences.en: Paul Rosen has been studying the psychology and culture of food for more than 40 years.
sentences.zh: 保罗·罗森研究食物心理学和文化已经超过40年了。

sentences.en: He works at the University of Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 他在宾夕法尼亚大学工作。

sentences.en: Early in his career, Paul found himself pondering a question that few of us might think to ask.
sentences.zh: 在职业生涯早期，保罗发现自己在思考一个我们很少有人会去想的问题。

sentences.en: Why do so many people across the world enjoy the hot, stinging pain of chili peppers?
sentences.zh: 为什么全世界有那么多人喜欢辣椒那种火辣、刺痛的感觉？

sentences.en: This question took Paul to a small village in Mexico where chili peppers were as common as salt and pepper in the United States.
sentences.zh: 这个问题把保罗带到了墨西哥的一个小村庄，在那里，辣椒就像美国的盐和胡椒一样普遍。

sentences.en: They don't think their food tastes good without it.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得没有辣椒，食物就不好吃。

sentences.en: And the little kids don't like it.
sentences.zh: 而小孩子并不喜欢它。

sentences.en: So something happens somewhere between two and five years of age.
sentences.zh: 所以，在两到五岁之间的某个阶段，发生了一些变化。

sentences.en: At the meals where everybody adult is eating the hot pepper and the older children are and they're all enjoying it and the little kid is thinking it's terrible.
sentences.zh: 在吃饭时，大人们都在吃辣椒，大一点的孩子也在吃，他们都很享受，而小孩子却觉得那太糟糕了。

sentences.en: And after a while, some magic occurs and the little kids like it.
sentences.zh: 过了一段时间，奇迹发生了，小孩子也喜欢上了它。

sentences.en: So I thought, well, we had a number of possible accounts.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时想，嗯，我们有几种可能的解释。

sentences.en: Some accounts involve something fundamentally biological.
sentences.zh: 有些解释涉及生物学层面的根本原因。

sentences.en: And presumably the biological explanation would be if you start eating it long enough, you're eventually just going to like it for biological reasons.
sentences.zh: 大概生物学上的解释是，如果你吃得够久，最终你会因为生物学原因而喜欢上它。

sentences.en: Yes, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: The brain compensates for all sorts of things.
sentences.zh: 大脑会补偿各种各样的事情。

sentences.en: We adapt to things.
sentences.zh: 我们会适应事物。

sentences.en: This is a case of more than adaptation where you're turning something that's negative into something positive.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是适应，你把负面的东西变成了正面的东西。

sentences.en: I mean, to me, that's an amazing thing that we can start with something that's innately negative and make it really positive.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对我来说，能够从天生负面的东西开始，并将其变得非常正面，这是一件了不起的事情。

sentences.en: So I said, let's take a look at the animals in the village because the dogs and the pigs eat Mexican food.
sentences.zh: 所以我说，让我们看看村里的动物，因为狗和猪也吃墨西哥食物。

sentences.en: They're eating tacos and hot sauce and beans and all of that stuff.
sentences.zh: 它们吃塔可、辣酱、豆子以及所有那些东西。

sentences.en: So I went around the village and I first asked people, do you have any dogs or pigs that like hot pepper?
sentences.zh: 所以我走遍了村子，首先问人们，你们有没有喜欢吃辣椒的狗或猪？

sentences.en: And they said, what, are you crazy?
sentences.zh: 他们说，什么，你疯了吗？

sentences.en: I said, well, yeah, I mean, they eat it.
sentences.zh: 我说，嗯，我是说，它们确实吃啊。

sentences.en: And they said, that's ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 他们说，那太荒谬了。

sentences.en: I said, would you mind if I give the dogs a little piece of cracker with some hot sauce on it and without and see what they choose?
sentences.zh: 我说，如果我给狗一块涂了辣酱的饼干，再给一块没涂的，看看它们选哪一个，你们介意吗？

sentences.en: So they said, go ahead.
sentences.zh: 他们说，请便。

sentences.en: And so I did go around the village with pigs and dogs.
sentences.zh: 于是我带着猪和狗在村子里做了实验。

sentences.en: I put out one cracker in front of them with hot pepper sauce and another without and I'd see what they did.
sentences.zh: 我在它们面前放了一块涂有辣椒酱的饼干和一块没涂的，看看它们会怎么做。

sentences.en: And it turns out that none of them ate the hot pepper firSt.
sentences.zh: 结果发现，它们没有一个先吃涂辣椒的。

sentences.en: They all ate the one with hot pepper because they're hungry.
sentences.zh: 它们都吃了涂辣椒的那块，因为它们饿了。

sentences.en: But their first choice was the one without hot pepper.
sentences.zh: 但它们的首选是没涂辣椒的那块。

sentences.en: So that I couldn't find an animal in the village that did what everyone over five years old and humans did, which was to gobble this stuff out and prefer it.
sentences.zh: 所以我无法在村里找到一种动物能像五岁以上的人类那样，狼吞虎咽地吃下这些东西并偏爱它。

sentences.en: So that suggested to me that it seems to be uniquely human.
sentences.zh: 这向我表明，这似乎是人类独有的。

sentences.en: And so this is not just a question of people getting used to it and getting to like it because the dogs and pigs are eating the garbage.
sentences.zh: 所以这不仅仅是人们习惯了并喜欢上它的问题，因为狗和猪也在吃垃圾。

sentences.en: The garbage is laced with chili peppers.
sentences.zh: 垃圾里混杂着辣椒。

sentences.en: If that was the case, that would be true for the animals as well.
sentences.zh: 如果真是那样的话，这对动物来说也应该适用。

sentences.en: So what was happening in the humans, in the human brain, if you will,
sentences.zh: 那么在人类身上，或者说在人类大脑中发生了什么，

sentences.en: that allowed five-year-old children to fall in love with chili peppers and kept their canine cousins from liking it?
sentences.zh: 使得五岁的孩子爱上了辣椒，却让它们的犬类同伴不喜欢它呢？

sentences.en: Well, that's indeed exactly the question.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这确实正是问题所在。

sentences.en: We don't know how this happens, but we do know that where it happens is at the meals where the kids are eating with their parents and their older siblings.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道这是如何发生的，但我们确实知道它发生的地方是在孩子们与父母和年长兄弟姐妹一起吃饭的时候。

sentences.en: And they keep eating it because there's social pressure to eat it.
sentences.zh: 他们继续吃是因为有社交压力。

sentences.en: Now, the animals keep eating it, too, because they're hungry.
sentences.zh: 现在，动物们也继续吃，因为它们饿了。

sentences.en: So it can't be just that they keep eating it.
sentences.zh: 所以不能仅仅是因为它们一直吃。

sentences.en: So it's really, to me, a miracle.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，这真是一个奇迹。

sentences.en: And what I realized is that it's a miracle that takes place in humans all over the world, not just about hot pepper.
sentences.zh: 我意识到，这是一个发生在全世界人类身上的奇迹，不仅仅是关于辣椒。

sentences.en: It's also about liking coffee, which is bitter.
sentences.zh: 这也关于喜欢咖啡，咖啡是苦的。

sentences.en: And people don't like it originally, and they like it.
sentences.zh: 人们起初不喜欢它，后来却喜欢上了。

sentences.en: And it goes outside the food domain.
sentences.zh: 而且这超出了食物领域。

sentences.en: People like to go on roller coasters.
sentences.zh: 人们喜欢坐过山车。

sentences.en: Now, a roller coaster is a very negative experience the first time you have it, right?
sentences.zh: 坐过山车第一次体验时是非常负面的经历，对吧？

sentences.en: You think you're crashing to death, and your heart is pounding, and yet people pay to do this.
sentences.zh: 你以为你要坠毁身亡，心跳加速，但人们还是花钱去坐。

sentences.en: Can you imagine a dog paying to go on a roller coaster?
sentences.zh: 你能想象一只狗花钱去坐过山车吗？

sentences.en: I mean, you know, it just won't happen.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，那是不可能发生的。

sentences.en: So we found that there's a whole range of things in which humans enjoy what is originally negative, and they come to enjoy it as positive.
sentences.zh: 所以我们发现，人类有一系列原本负面的事物，他们最终会将其视为正面并享受其中。

sentences.en: This includes the fatigue of running.
sentences.zh: 这包括跑步时的疲劳感。

sentences.en: It includes sad movies.
sentences.zh: 包括悲伤的电影。

sentences.en: It includes being afraid in horror movies.
sentences.zh: 包括看恐怖片时的恐惧感。

sentences.en: This seems to be only humans.
sentences.zh: 这似乎只有人类才会这样。

sentences.en: So our thought, and it's only a thought, is that what humans are enjoying is the very fact that their body thinks that something is bad, but they know it's okay.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的想法，仅仅是一个想法，是人类享受的正是这样一个事实：他们的身体认为某事很糟糕，但他们知道这没关系。

sentences.en: We call it benign masochism.
sentences.zh: 我们称之为良性受虐。

sentences.en: The humans have this special ability to appreciate the fact that they know that something that their body is saying is bad is actually good.
sentences.zh: 人类有一种特殊的能力，能够欣赏这样一个事实：他们知道身体所说的糟糕的事情实际上是好的。

sentences.en: And we have evidence for that.
sentences.zh: 我们有证据支持这一点。

sentences.en: So, for example, for chili pepper, the favorite degree of hotness is just below the level of unbearable pain.
sentences.zh: 例如，对于辣椒，人们最喜欢的辣度刚好在难以忍受的疼痛水平之下。

sentences.en: They're pushing as far as they can to get their body to really scream, get this out of here, and yet know that it's okay.
sentences.zh: 他们尽可能地逼迫自己，让身体尖叫着“把它弄出去”，但同时又知道这没关系。

sentences.en: So it seems to be a very general feature of humans, which we tapped into by asking why a couple of billion people like hot pepper.
sentences.zh: 所以这似乎是人类的一个非常普遍的特征，我们通过询问为什么几十亿人喜欢辣椒而发现了这一点。

sentences.en: So in some ways, the theory is that you start out not liking it, and then social pressure, if you will, convinces you to try it,
sentences.zh: 所以在某种程度上，理论是这样的：你起初不喜欢它，然后社交压力说服你去尝试，

sentences.en: and then you try it often enough that your body learns to adapt to it a little bit.
sentences.zh: 然后你尝试的次数足够多，你的身体学会了一点点适应它。

sentences.en: But then eventually you start to like it for actually a slightly different reason.
sentences.zh: 但最终你开始喜欢它，其实是因为一个稍微不同的原因。

sentences.en: You're no longer liking it just because of the peer pressure or the social interactions.
sentences.zh: 你不再仅仅是因为同伴压力或社交互动而喜欢它。

sentences.en: You're liking it because it gives you a sense that you're coming close to the edge of something thrilling.
sentences.zh: 你喜欢它是因为它让你感觉到自己正在接近某种令人兴奋的边缘。

sentences.en: Is that the argument?
sentences.zh: 这就是你的论点吗？

sentences.en: Yes, it's something thrilling that is not threatening.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一种令人兴奋但没有威胁感的东西。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, for example, if something is threatening, you don't get to like it.
sentences.zh: 所以，例如，如果某事是有威胁性的，你就不会喜欢它。

sentences.en: Like people don't get to like serious pain.
sentences.zh: 就像人们不会喜欢严重的疼痛一样。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It has to have something of the sense of it's not really threatening.
sentences.zh: 它必须有一种“它并非真的具有威胁性”的感觉。

sentences.en: And it even becomes funny.
sentences.zh: 甚至会变得有趣。

sentences.en: So in the case of disgust, people don't like disgusting things, right?
sentences.zh: 所以在厌恶的情况下，人们不喜欢令人作呕的东西，对吧？

sentences.en: But they make exceptions.
sentences.zh: 但他们会破例。

sentences.en: They eat smelly cheese, and they come to like that smell in the context of the cheese, even though their body is saying, get this out of your mouth.
sentences.zh: 他们吃臭奶酪，尽管身体在说“把它从嘴里弄出去”，但他们最终还是在奶酪的语境下喜欢上了那种味道。

sentences.en: It stinks.
sentences.zh: 它很臭。

sentences.en: You once performed an experiment on yourself.
sentences.zh: 你曾经在自己身上做过一个实验。

sentences.en: You were with your wife, I believe, at a Korean restaurant in New York City.
sentences.zh: 我相信当时你和你的妻子在纽约市的一家韩国餐馆。

sentences.en: And you did an interview with NPR back in 2015 where you told the reporter that it was one of the hottest things you'd ever eaten.
sentences.zh: 你在2015年接受NPR采访时告诉记者，那是你吃过的最辣的东西之一。

sentences.en: Tell me that story.
sentences.zh: 给我讲讲那个故事。

sentences.en: Well, my wife at the time was a cookbook writer, and she was very interested in cuisine.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我当时的妻子是一位食谱作家，她对烹饪非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: And we went to a Korean restaurant in New York.
sentences.zh: 我们去了纽约的一家韩国餐馆。

sentences.en: And the people around us, they were ordering some dish that we didn't recognize.
sentences.zh: 周围的人点了一道我们不认识的菜。

sentences.en: So we said to the waiter, we would like that.
sentences.zh: 所以我们对服务员说，我们想要那个。

sentences.en: And he says, you don't want that.
sentences.zh: 他说，你们不会想要那个的。

sentences.en: I said, no, no.
sentences.zh: 我说，不，不。

sentences.en: We said, we'd really like to try new foods.
sentences.zh: 我们说，我们真的很想尝试新食物。

sentences.en: He says, you don't want to try that food.
sentences.zh: 他说，你们不会想尝试那种食物的。

sentences.en: So this went on, and we won, of course.
sentences.zh: 所以这种情况持续了一会儿，当然，我们赢了。

sentences.en: And he brought this dish, and it was unbearably hot.
sentences.zh: 他端来了那道菜，辣得难以忍受。

sentences.en: And we ate it because we were shamed into eating it by our own insistence that it was good.
sentences.zh: 我们把它吃完了，因为我们坚持说它好吃，结果被自己的坚持给羞辱了。

sentences.en: I have another story of a different sort.
sentences.zh: 我还有另一个不同类型的故事。

sentences.en: It also happened in New York.
sentences.zh: 也发生在纽约。

sentences.en: I had a colleague who had a dog, and the dog liked to eat dog poop.
sentences.zh: 我有个同事养了条狗，那条狗喜欢吃狗屎。

sentences.en: So they would go into Washington Square Park with the dog, and the dog would just hunt out a dog poop and eat it.
sentences.zh: 所以他们会带着狗去华盛顿广场公园，狗就会到处寻找狗屎吃。

sentences.en: And it was just awful.
sentences.zh: 那真是太糟糕了。

sentences.en: You know, they hated it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们很讨厌这样。

sentences.en: The dog smelled it.
sentences.zh: 狗闻了闻它。

sentences.en: So they went to a vet, and the vet said, why don't you put hot pepper on the dog poop?
sentences.zh: 所以他们去看兽医，兽医说，为什么不在狗屎上撒点辣椒呢？

sentences.en: Because dogs don't like hot pepper.
sentences.zh: 因为狗不喜欢辣椒。

sentences.en: So they go into Washington Square.
sentences.zh: 于是他们去了华盛顿广场。

sentences.en: I want you to get this image.
sentences.zh: 我想让你想象一下这个画面。

sentences.en: Barbara's holding the dog on a leash, and her husband goes with a shaker of hot pepper, finds a dog turd, and seasons it in front of everybody with all this hot pepper.
sentences.zh: 芭芭拉牵着狗，她丈夫拿着一瓶辣椒粉，找到一坨狗屎，当着所有人的面给它撒上辣椒粉。

sentences.en: I mean, the idea of someone seasoning a dog turd is really pretty good.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有人给狗屎调味的想法真的很不错。

sentences.en: And then they let the dog go, and the dog ate it.
sentences.zh: 然后他们松开狗，狗还是把它吃了。

sentences.en: And did the dog stop eating dog poop?
sentences.zh: 那狗停止吃狗屎了吗？

sentences.en: No, no, because the dog liked dog poop more than it disliked the hotness.
sentences.zh: 没有，没有，因为狗喜欢狗屎胜过它讨厌辣味。

sentences.en: You know, people will put up with pain to do something they really like, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们为了做他们真正喜欢的事情会忍受痛苦，对吧？

sentences.en: Just as Paul has shown that the sense of taste is shaped by the brain, he's also done work that shows the same thing for appetite.
sentences.zh: 正如保罗所展示的那样，味觉是由大脑塑造的，他也做了同样的研究来证明食欲也是如此。

sentences.en: In one study, he sat a meal down before patients who had amnesia.
sentences.zh: 在一项研究中，他在患有健忘症的病人面前放了一顿饭。

sentences.en: Yes, the general view in most of the people who work on hunger is that hunger comes when, you know, your body reserves are low,
sentences.zh: 是的，大多数研究饥饿的人的普遍观点是，当你身体储备不足时，饥饿感就会产生，

sentences.en: maybe your blood glucose is low, various hormones come out, and you feel this sensation of hunger, and you eat until it disappears.
sentences.zh: 也许你的血糖很低，各种激素分泌出来，你就会感到饥饿，然后一直吃到饥饿感消失。

sentences.en: Now, there's some truth in that, of course, but there are many other higher order things.
sentences.zh: 当然，这其中有一定道理，但还有许多其他更高层面的因素。

sentences.en: So, for example, the cultural definition of what's a meal is very important.
sentences.zh: 比如，文化对“什么是正餐”的定义就非常重要。

sentences.en: After you finish the meal and have dessert, you stop eating.
sentences.zh: 吃完正餐，享用过甜点后，你就会停止进食。

sentences.en: So to try to show this, we dealt with two amnesic patients who were totally amnesic.
sentences.zh: 为了验证这一点，我们找了两位完全失忆的病人进行研究。

sentences.en: They didn't remember anything that happened more than 30 seconds ago, but they were quite intact otherwise.
sentences.zh: 他们记不住30秒前发生的任何事，但除此之外，他们的其他功能都很正常。

sentences.en: So we fed them lunch in a situation where they were in a room without a clock.
sentences.zh: 我们安排他们在没有时钟的房间里吃午餐。

sentences.en: And we said, lunchtime, and it was lunchtime, and we brought them a favorite lunch of theirs.
sentences.zh: 我们告诉他们“午餐时间到了”，当时确实也是午餐时间，然后给他们端上了他们最爱吃的午餐。

sentences.en: We'd ask them what their lunch was, and they, of course, ate it.
sentences.zh: 我们问他们午餐吃得怎么样，他们当然都吃完了。

sentences.en: Then we took the plate away.
sentences.zh: 接着我们把盘子收走。

sentences.en: There were no more signs that they'd eaten.
sentences.zh: 现场没有任何他们吃过东西的痕迹。

sentences.en: And 10 minutes later, we brought another lunch and said, lunchtime, and they all ate it three times each, the second lunch completely.
sentences.zh: 10分钟后，我们又端上另一份午餐，说“午餐时间到了”，结果他们每人都把第二份午餐也吃得干干净净，一共吃了三次。

sentences.en: Then we took that away, waited 10 minutes, and brought a third lunch.
sentences.zh: 然后我们收走盘子，等了10分钟，又端上了第三份午餐。

sentences.en: Each of these were full-size lunches.
sentences.zh: 每一份都是足量的午餐。

sentences.en: And most of the time, they ate the third lunch.
sentences.zh: 大多数情况下，他们连第三份午餐也吃掉了。

sentences.en: Twice, I think, one of them said, I'm getting a little stuffed, meaning their stomach was really getting full.
sentences.zh: 我想有两次，其中一个人说“我有点撑了”，意思是他们的胃确实已经满了。

sentences.en: But the point was that they're eating, when you're served a meal, if it looks palatable, you tend to eat it.
sentences.zh: 但重点在于，当你被端上一顿正餐时，如果它看起来很诱人，你往往就会吃下去。

sentences.en: I was on a plane once flying to Chicago, and at 3 in the afternoon, they served a full lunch.
sentences.zh: 有一次我坐飞机去芝加哥，下午3点的时候，他们供应了一顿完整的午餐。

sentences.en: Now, everyone had eaten lunch already, but six out of the nine people who I could see ate that lunch because it was lunch, and it was food, and it looked good.
sentences.zh: 当时每个人都已经吃过午餐了，但我能看到的9个人里有6个还是吃了那顿午餐，因为那是午餐，是食物，而且看起来不错。

sentences.en: Probably wasn't good if it was airplane food, but they ate it.
sentences.zh: 虽然如果是飞机餐的话，味道可能并不怎么样，但他们还是吃了。

sentences.en: So a lot of what we do is we eat when there's good food around and when the situation is appropriate.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们很多时候进食是因为周围有好吃的食物，而且当时的情况也合适。

sentences.en: Now, if we had left their first lunch and they saw the plate in front of them with pieces of chicken bone, they might have realized that I've just eaten.
sentences.zh: 如果当时我们没收走第一份午餐，让他们看到盘子里剩下的鸡骨头，他们可能就会意识到自己刚吃过东西。

sentences.en: And when we give normal people a second meal in the same way I just described, they don't say, I'm not hungry.
sentences.zh: 而当我们用同样的方式给普通人提供第二顿饭时，他们不会说“我不饿”。

sentences.en: They say, I just ate.
sentences.zh: 他们会说“我刚吃过”。

sentences.en: So it's fascinating because I think what you're saying really is that memory plays a huge role in whether we think we're hungry.
sentences.zh: 这太迷人了，因为我认为你所说的其实是：记忆在我们是否认为自己饥饿这件事上扮演了重要角色。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Being hungry is only one reason that we eat.
sentences.zh: 饥饿只是我们进食的原因之一。

sentences.en: So if you go for a full dinner, halfway through that dinner, you're not hungry anymore.
sentences.zh: 如果你去吃一顿丰盛的晚餐，吃到一半时，你其实已经不饿了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But you're still eating the rest of the meal.
sentences.zh: 但你还是会把剩下的饭菜吃完。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So hunger can't institute meals.
sentences.zh: 所以饥饿感并不能决定正餐的开始。

sentences.en: The lack of it will probably discourage you from eating more, but there are other things that influence you too.
sentences.zh: 没有饥饿感可能会让你不想再吃，但还有其他因素在影响你。

sentences.en: When we come back, the role that culture plays in our experience of food, we'll also look at how you can serve more memorable meals.
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，我们将探讨文化在我们饮食体验中扮演的角色，并看看如何提供更令人难忘的餐点。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》（Hidden Brain）。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆（Shankar Vedantam）。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: I'm talking with psychologist Paul Rosen, who has spent many decades examining the interplay between food, identity, and culture.
sentences.zh: 我正在与心理学家保罗·罗森（Paul Rosen）交谈，他几十年来一直致力于研究食物、身份认同与文化之间的相互作用。

sentences.en: Food is not just nutrition that goes in your mouth or even pleasant sensations that go with it.
sentences.zh: 食物不仅仅是进入你口中的营养，甚至也不仅仅是随之而来的愉悦感。

sentences.en: It connects to your whole life.
sentences.zh: 它与你的整个人生息息相关。

sentences.en: And it's really a very important part of performing your culture and experiencing your culture.
sentences.zh: 它是展现文化和体验文化非常重要的一部分。

sentences.en: When Paul asked people about their favorite meals, they certainly mentioned eating at great restaurants.
sentences.zh: 当保罗问人们关于他们最喜欢的餐点时，他们当然提到了在高级餐厅用餐的经历。

sentences.en: But they also talk about memories of meals that they shared with family and friends.
sentences.zh: 但他们也谈到了与家人和朋友分享餐点的记忆。

sentences.en: Here's a very common answer that's very short.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个非常简短的常见回答。

sentences.en: For a home meal.
sentences.zh: 关于家常菜。

sentences.en: Every Christmas Eve, my Italian grandfather and Greek grandmother would cook a meal consisting of creamy carbonara with bacon pieces throughout, homemade spinach pie, and sausage.
sentences.zh: 每个平安夜，我的意大利爷爷和希腊奶奶都会做一顿大餐，包括混有培根碎的奶油培根面、自制菠菜派和香肠。

sentences.en: It was always amazing.
sentences.zh: 那总是棒极了。

sentences.en: Now, that's a lovely one, right?
sentences.zh: 听起来很棒，对吧？

sentences.en: And it's not fancy, but you can see the emotion and the pleasure of it.
sentences.zh: 它并不奢华，但你能感受到其中的情感和愉悦。

sentences.en: And it's connected, of course, to the pleasure of family, not just to the pleasure of food.
sentences.zh: 而且它当然与家庭的快乐联系在一起，而不仅仅是食物带来的快乐。

sentences.en: Yes, it's very social.
sentences.zh: 是的，这非常有社交属性。

sentences.en: Pleasure is only one factor when it comes to what we eat and how much we eat.
sentences.zh: 当我们谈论吃什么和吃多少时，愉悦感只是其中一个因素。

sentences.en: Contrast and context can be important.
sentences.zh: 对比和情境也很重要。

sentences.en: Consider the difference between a tapas-style meal and a meal that's built around one large entree.
sentences.zh: 考虑一下西班牙小吃（tapas）风格的餐点与以一道大主菜为核心的餐点之间的区别。

sentences.en: In both cases, you can fill up your stomach.
sentences.zh: 在这两种情况下，你都能填饱肚子。

sentences.en: But it turns out these have very different effects on your brain.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，它们对你的大脑有着截然不同的影响。

sentences.en: As social scientists have found, most of us find it difficult to tell the difference between the tenth bite and the eleventh bite of the very same food.
sentences.zh: 正如社会科学家所发现的那样，我们大多数人很难分辨出同一种食物的第十口和第十一口有什么区别。

sentences.en: There's a whole line of modern decision research, most associated with Daniel Kahneman, who got a Nobel Prize for it, and Amos Tversky,
sentences.zh: 有一整套现代决策研究，主要与获得诺贝尔奖的丹尼尔·卡尼曼（Daniel Kahneman）和阿莫斯·特沃斯基（Amos Tversky）有关，

sentences.en: showing that people are not so rational as you might expect them to be.
sentences.zh: 他们表明人们并不像你想象的那么理性。

sentences.en: And one of the features of it is called duration neglect, which is people don't remember how long an experience is.
sentences.zh: 其中一个特征被称为“持续时间忽视”（duration neglect），即人们记不住一段经历持续了多久。

sentences.en: They just remember the experience.
sentences.zh: 他们只记得这段经历本身。

sentences.en: So if you had a pain for 12 hours or a pain for one hour, two weeks later, what you remember is the experience of the pain, not how long it was.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你忍受了12小时的疼痛或1小时的疼痛，两周后，你记住的是疼痛的经历，而不是它持续了多久。

sentences.en: So this applied to food means that if you have the same food, a lot of the same food,
sentences.zh: 因此，这应用到食物上意味着，如果你吃同样的食物，吃很多同样的食物，

sentences.en: it won't produce a very different memory from having a little of that same food because it's the memory of eating the food.
sentences.zh: 它产生的记忆与只吃一点点同样的食物并不会有太大区别，因为记忆的是“吃这种食物”的体验。

sentences.en: So this raises a very important question that Kahneman originally brought up, which is the distinction between your experience and your memory for the experience.
sentences.zh: 这提出了一个卡尼曼最初提出的非常重要的问题，即你的“体验自我”与“记忆自我”之间的区别。

sentences.en: Kahneman and others have shown, we've done some work on this too, that the ending of an experience is particularly important.
sentences.zh: 卡尼曼和其他人已经证明——我们也做过一些相关研究——一段经历的结尾尤为重要。

sentences.en: So when you remember something, you're more likely to remember the end of it.
sentences.zh: 所以当你回忆某件事时，你更有可能记住它的结尾。

sentences.en: And also, by the way, to some extent, more likely to remember the beginning of it.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，在某种程度上，你也更有可能记住它的开头。

sentences.en: And that would mean if you want to produce the best memory for food, you should put the best foods at the beginning and the end.
sentences.zh: 这意味着如果你想创造关于食物的最佳记忆，你应该把最好的食物放在开头和结尾。

sentences.en: Whereas most people think the entree is the best, which is in the middle and is the least remembered.
sentences.zh: 而大多数人认为主菜是最好的，但它位于中间，也是最容易被遗忘的部分。

sentences.en: We had Danny Kahneman on Hidden Brain recently.
sentences.zh: 我们最近在《隐藏的大脑》节目中邀请了丹尼·卡尼曼。

sentences.en: And, of course, you talked about the peak-end rule and also about the difference between the experiencing self and the remembering self.
sentences.zh: 当然，你谈到了“峰终定律”（peak-end rule），以及“体验自我”和“记忆自我”之间的区别。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And one of the implications of this, as you point out, this difference between experiencing a meal and remembering a meal,
sentences.zh: 正如你所指出的，这种体验一顿饭与记忆一顿饭之间的区别，其含义之一是，

sentences.en: is it points to the difference between people who go to restaurants and order their favorite dish every time
sentences.zh: 它揭示了那些去餐厅每次都点最爱菜肴的人，

sentences.en: and people who go to a restaurant and order a new dish every time.
sentences.zh: 与那些去餐厅每次都点新菜肴的人之间的区别。

sentences.en: How are these two strategies essentially catering to two different psychological impulses?
sentences.zh: 这两种策略本质上是如何迎合两种不同的心理冲动的？

sentences.en: Well, that's an issue that we have looked at, and it's pretty clear.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是我们研究过的一个问题，答案很明确。

sentences.en: If you're going to order your favorite food, and you know you're going to order that before you go to the restaurant,
sentences.zh: 如果你打算点你最喜欢的食物，而且在去餐厅之前就知道自己要点什么，

sentences.en: there are actually three aspects.
sentences.zh: 实际上有三个方面。

sentences.en: There's your anticipation.
sentences.zh: 即你的期待、体验和记忆。

sentences.en: This comes from Kahneman.
sentences.zh: 这来自卡尼曼的理论。

sentences.en: The anticipation, the experience, and the memory.
sentences.zh: 期待、体验和记忆。

sentences.en: Your anticipation of a meal is going to be higher if you order your favorite food
sentences.zh: 如果你点的是最喜欢的食物，你对这顿饭的期待会更高，

sentences.en: because you know you're going to have something great, right?
sentences.zh: 因为你知道你会吃到很棒的东西，对吧？

sentences.en: Whereas if you can order something new, it's not even clear what you can imagine
sentences.zh: 而如果你点新菜，你甚至不知道该想象什么，

sentences.en: because you don't know what it is.
sentences.zh: 因为你不知道它是什么。

sentences.en: At the meal itself, you're probably going to enjoy your favorite dish more than a new dish
sentences.zh: 在用餐时，你可能比吃新菜更能享受你最喜欢的菜肴，

sentences.en: because it's one of their best dishes.
sentences.zh: 因为那是他们最好的菜之一。

sentences.en: You love it.
sentences.zh: 你很喜欢它。

sentences.en: There's a little risk in ordering something new.
sentences.zh: 点新菜是有一定风险的。

sentences.en: But if you order your favorite dish, you're not going to create a new memory.
sentences.zh: 但如果你点最喜欢的菜，你就不会创造新的记忆。

sentences.en: Whereas if you order a new food, you're going to create a new memory.
sentences.zh: 而如果你点新食物，你就会创造新的记忆。

sentences.en: We are looking at this, but we don't know yet for sure.
sentences.zh: 我们正在研究这一点，但目前还不能完全确定。

sentences.en: If you're a person who generally values memories,
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个通常看重记忆的人，

sentences.en: then you're going to try to create more memories by creating new experiences.
sentences.zh: 那么你就会尝试通过创造新的体验来创造更多的记忆。

sentences.en: Whereas if you value anticipation and experience more,
sentences.zh: 而如果你更看重期待和体验，

sentences.en: you will keep doing the same wonderful thing.
sentences.zh: 你就会继续做同样美妙的事情。

sentences.en: So how you value anticipation, memory, and experience
sentences.zh: 所以你如何权衡期待、记忆和体验，

sentences.en: affects how you're going to choose what activities you do.
sentences.zh: 会影响你如何选择自己要做的事情。

sentences.en: Let's just take an example.
sentences.zh: 我们举个例子。

sentences.en: Massage.
sentences.zh: 按摩。

sentences.en: I like massage.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢按摩。

sentences.en: I go once a month, I get a massage.
sentences.zh: 我每个月去一次，做一次按摩。

sentences.en: It's pretty much the same.
sentences.zh: 基本上都差不多。

sentences.en: I can't tell you last month's massage was exactly this.
sentences.zh: 我无法告诉你上个月的按摩具体是什么样的。

sentences.en: So I'm going for the anticipation and the experience, which is very positive.
sentences.zh: 所以我追求的是期待和体验，这非常积极。

sentences.en: I don't really create much memory from this.
sentences.zh: 我并没有从中创造出多少记忆。

sentences.en: And I do it and I like it, but it's very different from the way I eat,
sentences.zh: 我做了，我也喜欢，但这和我吃东西的方式非常不同，

sentences.en: where I'm always trying to say I want to enrich my mental menu listing,
sentences.zh: 我总是试图丰富我的“心理菜单列表”，

sentences.en: you know, my life experience of food.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我关于食物的人生体验。

sentences.en: But people differ on this.
sentences.zh: 但人们在这方面各不相同。

sentences.en: We've been interested in trying to see if people are consistently different.
sentences.zh: 我们一直有兴趣看看人们是否在这些方面表现出一致的差异。

sentences.en: We don't know yet.
sentences.zh: 我们还不知道。

sentences.en: Think of a seven-day Caribbean vacation at a resort.
sentences.zh: 想想在度假村度过的七天加勒比海假期。

sentences.en: Almost nothing happens, right?
sentences.zh: 几乎什么都没发生，对吧？

sentences.en: You're feeling good.
sentences.zh: 你感觉很好。

sentences.en: The sun is good.
sentences.zh: 阳光很好。

sentences.en: You go in the water.
sentences.zh: 你去水里玩。

sentences.en: It's nice.
sentences.zh: 很不错。

sentences.en: But there's no...
sentences.zh: 但没有……

sentences.en: If people say, tell me about your vacation, it's going to be a very short thing, right?
sentences.zh: 如果有人问你，跟我说说你的假期，那会是一个非常简短的回答，对吧？

sentences.en: So there's two kinds of vacations.
sentences.zh: 所以有两种假期。

sentences.en: Those that are really high on experience and vacations that will give you a lot of experience,
sentences.zh: 一种是体验感极强的假期，会给你带来很多体验，

sentences.en: but there'll also be some hardship.
sentences.zh: 但也会伴随着一些艰辛。

sentences.en: You'll get tired.
sentences.zh: 你会感到疲惫。

sentences.en: Something may not work.
sentences.zh: 有些事情可能不顺利。

sentences.en: Something might be closed when you thought it was open.
sentences.zh: 你以为开门的地方可能关门了。

sentences.en: All kinds of things can happen, so it won't be a totally positive experience,
sentences.zh: 各种各样的事情都可能发生，所以它不会是一次完全积极的体验，

sentences.en: but it will be a bunch of good memories.
sentences.zh: 但它会留下一堆美好的回忆。

sentences.en: You've thought a lot about the differences between the American attitude toward food
sentences.zh: 你深入思考过美国人对食物的态度与法国人对食物的态度之间的差异，

sentences.en: and the French attitude toward food,
sentences.zh: 你说法国人更关注嘴里的感受，

sentences.en: and you say that the French are more focused on what happens in the mouth,
sentences.zh: 而美国人往往更关注血液里的成分。

sentences.en: and Americans are often more focused by what happens in the bloodstream.
sentences.zh: 我想给你放一段简短的电影片段，来说明这个观点。

sentences.en: I want to play you a short movie clip that illustrates this idea.

sentences.zh: 如果我们总是担心食物，那也没关系，

sentences.zh: 但我们似乎在担心食物，而不是活得更久，

sentences.zh: 所以这看起来像是一笔糟糕的交易。

sentences.en: So we started a study of how French and Americans differ in the way they eat.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们开始研究法国人和美国人在饮食方式上有何不同。

sentences.en: And it's basically got two parts to it.
sentences.zh: 这项研究基本上分为两部分。

sentences.en: One is how they think about food,
sentences.zh: 一是他们如何看待食物，

sentences.en: and the other is how their food world is set up.
sentences.zh: 二是他们的饮食环境是如何设置的。

sentences.en: The French think about food as an oral experience.
sentences.zh: 法国人将食物视为一种口腔体验。

sentences.en: They think about eating as something that is giving them pleasure.
sentences.zh: 他们认为进食是一件能带给他们愉悦的事情。

sentences.en: They don't tend to think about what's going into their bloodstream,
sentences.zh: 他们往往不会去想什么东西进入了他们的血液，

sentences.en: how much sugar is in their animal fat.
sentences.zh: 或者动物脂肪里有多少糖分。

sentences.en: So they're getting more pleasure out of food because they're not worrying about it.
sentences.zh: 所以他们从食物中获得了更多的快乐，因为他们并不为此担忧。

sentences.en: So, for example, if we ask French,
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，如果我们问法国人，

sentences.en: when you think of heavy cream, do you think of whipped or unhealthy?
sentences.zh: 当你想到浓奶油时，你会想到它是搅打过的还是不健康的？

sentences.en: They will say usually whipped, and Americans will say unhealthy.
sentences.zh: 他们通常会说是搅打过的，而美国人会说是“不健康”。

sentences.en: Now, it's the same thing, but they're thinking about it as an experience,
sentences.zh: 其实这是同一样东西，但他们将其视为一种体验，

sentences.en: and we're thinking about it more as a health event.
sentences.zh: 而我们更多地将其视为一种健康事件。

sentences.en: And in some ways that actually might be a good thing, right?
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，这实际上可能是一件好事，对吧？

sentences.en: Because presumably when you take more pleasure in food,
sentences.zh: 因为据推测，当你从食物中获得更多快乐时，

sentences.en: you're focused on it.
sentences.zh: 你会专注于它。

sentences.en: You're not necessarily just focused on getting stuff in your mouth
sentences.zh: 你未必只是专注于把东西塞进嘴里，

sentences.en: or focusing on nutrition.
sentences.zh: 或者专注于营养成分。

sentences.en: The French, for example, seem to pay more attention to portion control than Americans,
sentences.zh: 例如，法国人似乎比美国人更注意份量控制，

sentences.en: except that I don't know if they're thinking about this as control.
sentences.zh: 只不过我不知道他们是否将其视为一种“控制”。

sentences.en: They're thinking about this as the enjoyment of food,
sentences.zh: 他们将其视为对食物的享受，

sentences.en: and once I'm done enjoying this bite, I'm done with it.
sentences.zh: 一旦我享受完了这一口，我就满足了。

sentences.en: Well, they eat more slowly, first of all.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，他们吃得更慢。

sentences.en: So they have more mouth experience
sentences.zh: 所以他们有更多的口腔体验，

sentences.en: because they don't swallow as quickly.
sentences.zh: 因为他们吞咽得没那么快。

sentences.en: They savor the food.
sentences.zh: 他们细细品味食物。

sentences.en: So, I mean, if you have a chocolate bar, you can bolt it down in a couple of minutes
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，如果你有一块巧克力，你可以几分钟内狼吞虎咽地吃完，

sentences.en: or you can make a 10 or 15-minute experience out of it.
sentences.zh: 或者你可以把它变成一种持续10到15分钟的体验。

sentences.en: And they're more inclined to the latter.
sentences.zh: 而他们更倾向于后者。

sentences.en: We actually were able to measure how, in McDonald's in Paris,
sentences.zh: 我们实际上能够测量出，在巴黎的麦当劳里，

sentences.en: how long people sat and ate compared to McDonald's in the United States, okay?
sentences.zh: 人们坐着吃饭的时间与美国麦当劳相比如何，好吗？

sentences.en: And we made sure there were French people in McDonald's.
sentences.zh: 而且我们确保了麦当劳里确实有法国人。

sentences.en: They were talking French.
sentences.zh: 他们在说法语。

sentences.en: The French people sitting in McDonald's sit there for longer
sentences.zh: 坐在麦当劳里的法国人坐的时间，

sentences.en: than the American people sit in McDonald's.
sentences.zh: 比坐在麦当劳里的美国人要长。

sentences.en: So they're eating more slowly.
sentences.zh: 所以他们吃得更慢。

sentences.en: They're talking more.
sentences.zh: 他们聊得更多。

sentences.en: You know, they're not just bolting down food.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们不仅仅是在狼吞虎咽地吃东西。

sentences.en: Food is not fuel.
sentences.zh: 食物不是燃料。

sentences.en: Americans often, not always, treat food as fuel,
sentences.zh: 美国人通常（并非总是）把食物当作燃料，

sentences.en: whereas the French think about it not as a fueling,
sentences.zh: 而法国人认为它不是一种补给，

sentences.en: but as an event and experience.
sentences.zh: 而是一场事件和一种体验。

sentences.en: Now, in the food world,
sentences.zh: 现在，在饮食世界里，

sentences.zh: 法国人和美国人之间最大的区别在于份量大小。

sentences.en: French traditionally serve smaller portions.

sentences.zh: 四人份的肉量，人均比美国食谱要少。

sentences.zh: 在法国的麦当劳，份量也更小。

sentences.en: Now, if you remember our discussion of the fact that you eat what's in front of you,
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你还记得我们讨论过的事实，即你会吃掉眼前的东西，

sentences.en: if it's pleasant, the amnesic patients,
sentences.zh: 如果它很可口的话，就像那些失忆症患者一样，

sentences.zh: 法国人摆在你面前的食物更少，

sentences.zh: 所以他们吃得更少，却享受得更多。

sentences.en: And that seems to me to be a good formula.
sentences.zh: 这在我看来是一个很好的公式。

sentences.en: Now, they have other features of it.
sentences.zh: 此外，他们还有其他特点。

sentences.en: The French meal is a much more elaborate event.
sentences.zh: 法国人的正餐是一场更精致的活动。

sentences.en: People don't get up, especially at home.
sentences.zh: 人们不会起身，尤其是在家里。

sentences.en: They don't get up in the middle of the meal and just leave the table.
sentences.zh: 他们不会在用餐中途就离开餐桌。

sentences.en: Everybody eats the same thing.
sentences.zh: 每个人都吃同样的东西。

sentences.en: So it's a social event.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种社交活动。

sentences.en: So, I would say the French deal with food well in the face of the modern world,
sentences.zh: 因此，我会说法国人在现代世界中处理食物的方式很好，

sentences.en: where there's so much good food around that we can easily stuff ourselves and eat everything under the sun.
sentences.zh: 在那个到处都是美食、我们很容易暴饮暴食并吃下一切的世界里。

sentences.en: They have managed to have a tradition which keeps it moderate and very pleasant.
sentences.zh: 他们成功地保留了一种传统，使其保持适度且非常愉悦。

sentences.zh: 保罗·罗森（Paul Rosen）研究食物的心理学和文化已经超过40年了。

sentences.en: There's a simple explanation for why we have the emotion of disguSt.
sentences.zh: 对于我们为什么会有厌恶这种情绪，有一个简单的解释。

sentences.en: It's a defense mechanism against things that could contaminate us.
sentences.zh: 这是一种针对可能污染我们的事物的防御机制。

sentences.en: But we often have flawed intuitions about how disgust works,
sentences.zh: 但我们对厌恶如何运作的直觉往往是有缺陷的，

sentences.en: starting with what's clean and what's dirty.
sentences.zh: 从什么是干净、什么是肮脏开始。

sentences.en: In her book, That's Disgusting, psychologist Rachel Herz talks about how the cleanliness of toilet seats
sentences.zh: 心理学家瑞秋·赫兹在她的书《那真恶心》（That's Disgusting）中谈到了马桶座圈的清洁度

sentences.en: compares to buttons on an ATM.
sentences.zh: 与自动取款机（ATM）按钮相比如何。

sentences.en: Things that we actually touch a lot and have no idea or don't really think about how disgusting they are,
sentences.zh: 那些我们实际上经常触摸，却完全不知道或根本不去想它们有多恶心的东西，

sentences.en: things like ATM buttons, actually our cell phones are just petri dishes of pathogens and germs,
sentences.zh: 比如ATM按钮，实际上我们的手机就是病原体和细菌的培养皿，

sentences.en: and most of us do not clean our cell phones very often.
sentences.zh: 而且我们大多数人并不经常清洁手机。

sentences.en: And yet we have this idea, because of the associations that we know very specifically between toilets
sentences.zh: 然而我们却有这样一种观念，因为我们非常清楚厕所

sentences.en: and waste from the human body, that toilets are really, really filthy,
sentences.zh: 与人体排泄物之间的联系，所以认为厕所真的非常非常肮脏，

sentences.en: and yet we don't give a second thought to things like keyboards or cell phones
sentences.zh: 但我们却从不考虑键盘或手机这类东西，

sentences.en: and other sorts of things that people are touching all the time and could be very dirty and contagious.
sentences.zh: 以及人们一直在触摸、可能非常肮脏且具有传染性的其他各种东西。

sentences.en: I want to talk about a certain quality that disgusting things have, Rachel,
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈厌恶事物所具有的一种特定品质，瑞秋，

sentences.en: which is that they tend to almost infect the things around them.
sentences.zh: 那就是它们几乎会感染周围的事物。

sentences.en: As the psychologist Paul Rosen, who's done a lot of work on disgust, says,
sentences.zh: 正如在厌恶研究方面做了大量工作的心理学家保罗·罗森所说，

sentences.en: a single cockroach will destroy the appeal of a bowl of cherries,
sentences.zh: 一只蟑螂会毁掉一碗樱桃的吸引力，

sentences.en: but a single cherry doesn't make a bowl of cockroaches appealing.
sentences.zh: 但一颗樱桃并不能让一碗蟑螂变得有吸引力。

sentences.en: Why do disgusting things infect the things around them?
sentences.zh: 为什么令人厌恶的事物会感染周围的事物？

sentences.en: Well, first I want to make a sort of flesh out a point there that I think is really interesting,
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先我想阐述一个我认为非常有趣的观点，

sentences.en: and that is that good does not overpower evil the way evil can overpower good.
sentences.zh: 那就是“善”并不能像“恶”压倒“善”那样去压倒“恶”。

sentences.en: And so, in fact, in other experiments, he found that the idea, for instance,
sentences.zh: 事实上，在其他实验中，他发现了一个想法，例如，

sentences.en: of how could you purify something like Hitler's sweater?
sentences.zh: 你如何净化像希特勒穿过的毛衣这样的东西？

sentences.en: So people are told that Hitler owned this sweater,
sentences.zh: 人们被告知希特勒拥有这件毛衣，

sentences.en: and would you be willing to wear it under varying conditions,
sentences.zh: 你是否愿意在不同条件下穿它，

sentences.en: or when could it become okay?
sentences.zh: 或者它在什么时候可以变得没问题？

sentences.en: And no form of cleaning could make it okay.
sentences.zh: 没有任何形式的清洁能让它变得没问题。

sentences.en: Mother Teresa wearing it could make it a little bit okay.
sentences.zh: 特蕾莎修女穿过它可能会让它稍微好一点。

sentences.en: But in the case of Hitler's sweater,
sentences.zh: 但在希特勒毛衣的案例中，

sentences.en: it had to be totally destroyed and burned in order for it to be okay.
sentences.zh: 它必须被彻底销毁和烧毁，才能变得没问题。

sentences.en: So good does not sanctify bad in the way that bad can sanctify good,
sentences.zh: 所以“善”不能像“恶”净化“善”那样去净化“恶”，

sentences.en: whereas just one spot of something bad, like a cockroach, for instance,
sentences.zh: 而仅仅是一点点坏东西，比如一只蟑螂，

sentences.en: in a glass of water or milk or anything else,
sentences.zh: 掉进一杯水或牛奶或其他任何东西里，

sentences.en: has the capacity to destroy the whole thing,
sentences.zh: 就有能力毁掉整个东西，

sentences.en: because negativity is much more pervasive and powerful from the way that we are built.
sentences.zh: 因为从我们的生理构造来看，负面影响更具渗透性和力量。

sentences.en: And this is, in fact, adaptive,
sentences.zh: 事实上，这是一种适应性，

sentences.en: because it's better to be worried about things that can harm us
sentences.zh: 因为担心可能伤害我们的事物，

sentences.en: than overly excited about things that might be benevolent.
sentences.zh: 总比对可能仁慈的事物过度兴奋要好。

sentences.en: I remember doing a story some years ago, Rachel,
sentences.zh: 我记得几年前做过一个报道，瑞秋，

sentences.en: that looked at a slightly related idea.
sentences.zh: 探讨了一个稍微相关的想法。

sentences.en: This was a work by the sociologist Ann Bowers,
sentences.zh: 这是社会学家安·鲍尔斯（Ann Bowers）的一项研究，

sentences.en: and she was studying the market for used wedding rings.
sentences.zh: 她当时正在研究二手结婚戒指的市场。

sentences.en: And she found that people were really reluctant to buy a wedding ring
sentences.zh: 她发现人们非常不愿意购买结婚戒指，

sentences.en: when they learned that the couple who had previously owned that wedding ring
sentences.zh: 当他们得知之前拥有那枚戒指的夫妇

sentences.en: had gotten divorced.
sentences.zh: 已经离婚时。

sentences.en: And people tended to want wedding rings where, you know,
sentences.zh: 人们往往更倾向于那些，你知道的，

sentences.en: there had been some tragic love story,
sentences.zh: 有过一段悲剧爱情故事，

sentences.en: but the couple had been very happy together.
sentences.zh: 但那对夫妇曾经非常幸福的结婚戒指。

sentences.en: So I'm not sure if it's exactly the same concept,
sentences.zh: 所以我不太确定这是否完全是同一个概念，

sentences.en: but it really feels as if inanimate objects can sometimes carry with them
sentences.zh: 但它确实让人感觉无生命的物体有时可以携带，

sentences.en: the, I don't know, the spirit, if you will.
sentences.zh: 怎么说呢，某种精神，如果你愿意这么称呼的话。

sentences.en: It's an unscientific idea.
sentences.zh: 这是一个不科学的想法。

sentences.en: The spirit of living things.
sentences.zh: 生物的精神。

sentences.en: Well, actually, it is very much the same concept, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 嗯，实际上，这确实是非常相同的概念，尚卡尔。

sentences.en: And what you're talking about is something called sympathetic magic,
sentences.zh: 你所谈论的是一种被称为“交感巫术”的东西，

sentences.en: which definitely plays a role in disgust
sentences.zh: 它绝对在厌恶中发挥了作用，

sentences.en: and what we're disgusted by through association.
sentences.zh: 以及我们通过联想而感到厌恶的事物。

sentences.en: The idea of once in contact, always in contact.
sentences.zh: 即“一旦接触，永远接触”的观念。

sentences.en: So, for example, the ring that was on the finger of the woman
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，那枚戴在一位女性手指上的戒指，

sentences.en: who had a terrible marriage and ended up getting divorced,
sentences.zh: 她经历了一段糟糕的婚姻并最终离婚了，

sentences.en: somehow, even though that ring is now in a jewelry shop,
sentences.zh: 不知何故，尽管那枚戒指现在在珠宝店里，

sentences.en: has nothing to do with that original couple whatsoever,
sentences.zh: 与最初的那对夫妇毫无关系，

sentences.en: the essence of that bad marriage is somehow still in the ring.
sentences.zh: 那段糟糕婚姻的本质不知何故仍然存在于戒指中。

sentences.en: And therefore, wearing that ring will therefore impart the bad marriage onto the new wearer.
sentences.zh: 因此，佩戴那枚戒指会将那段糟糕的婚姻传给新的佩戴者。

sentences.en: And somehow this spirit, as you said, will transcend and infect the new marriage.
sentences.zh: 不知何故，这种精神，正如你所说，会超越并感染新的婚姻。

sentences.en: So, again, it's a form of infection.
sentences.zh: 所以，这又是一种感染形式。

sentences.en: You have a very simple and interesting thought experiment in your book,
sentences.zh: 你的书里有一个非常简单且有趣的思维实验，

sentences.en: which is I'm not disgusted at the thought that when I drink a glass of water that there is saliva in my mouth.
sentences.zh: 那就是，当我喝一杯水时，想到我嘴里有唾液，我并不感到厌恶。

sentences.en: But if I spit in a glass of water and then I drink that glass of water, that seems disgusting.
sentences.zh: 但如果我往杯子里吐口水，然后再喝那杯水，那看起来就很恶心。

sentences.en: And, of course, in both cases, it's exactly the same outcome.
sentences.zh: 当然，在这两种情况下，结果完全一样。

sentences.en: I have water in my mouth with saliva in my mouth.
sentences.zh: 我嘴里有水，也有唾液。

sentences.en: Why does it feel more disgusting in one case and not the other?
sentences.zh: 为什么一种情况让人觉得更恶心，而另一种却不会？

sentences.en: So, that's exactly a great point about the idea that disgust is about the outside coming in and contaminating our inside.
sentences.zh: 所以，关于“厌恶感源于外部事物进入并污染了我们的内部”这一观点，这确实是一个很好的切入点。

sentences.en: So, while the saliva in the water is in our mouth, it's inside of us.
sentences.zh: 因此，当水里的唾液还在我们嘴里时，它属于我们身体的一部分。

sentences.en: And even just take water out of the equation, just the fact that you have saliva in your mouth right now,
sentences.zh: 甚至撇开水不谈，单就你现在嘴里有唾液这件事来说，

sentences.en: we're all okay with that.
sentences.zh: 我们对此都觉得没问题。

sentences.en: But as soon as we spit that exact same saliva that's in our mouth into the glass and then look at that and then I'm telling you now you should drink that,
sentences.zh: 但一旦我们把嘴里那同样的唾液吐进杯子里，看着它，然后我现在告诉你你应该喝下去，

sentences.en: it all of a sudden, even though it's only been out in the air for seconds, has become contaminated by the outside.
sentences.zh: 它突然之间——尽管暴露在空气中才几秒钟——就被外部环境污染了。

sentences.en: And bringing it back into our body is now an entirely different proposition.
sentences.zh: 而把它重新带回我们的身体，现在就成了完全不同的另一回事了。

sentences.en: And the fact also, I think in this case, that even though I know it's my saliva, it could be your saliva, it could be anybody else's saliva,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，在这种情况下，尽管我知道那是我的唾液，它也可能是你的，或者是任何其他人的唾液，

sentences.en: suddenly it becomes equalized with all the saliva that I know is out there that I definitely do not want in my mouth.
sentences.zh: 它突然就变得和我所知道的那些我绝对不想放进嘴里的唾液等同起来了。

sentences.en: So, if someone, for instance, is talking at you and spitting while they're talking, you know, enthusiastically,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果有人在和你说话时，因为情绪激动而喷出唾沫，

sentences.en: we're disgusted by the fact that some spit could touch us.
sentences.zh: 我们会被唾沫可能溅到我们身上这一事实感到恶心。

sentences.en: Just like once our spit is outside of our mouth, it becomes much less pleasant to think about taking it back in.
sentences.zh: 就像一旦我们的唾液离开了口腔，再想把它咽回去就会让人觉得很不舒服。

sentences.en: There was a really interesting study done about sharing your toothbrush.
sentences.zh: 有一个关于共用牙刷的非常有趣的实验。

sentences.en: And this study found that, so again, the idea that, you know, you're having to have something in your mouth that somebody else had in their mouth.
sentences.zh: 这个实验发现，同样是关于“你不得不把别人放进嘴里的东西再放进自己嘴里”这一想法，

sentences.en: And it was found that the person that one would least like to share your toothbrush with is the boss that you don't like.
sentences.zh: 研究发现，人们最不想共用牙刷的对象是你讨厌的老板。

sentences.en: Followed by, so if you don't like your boss, you definitely do not want to share your toothbrush with him or her.
sentences.zh: 其次是，如果你不喜欢你的老板，你绝对不想和他或她共用牙刷。

sentences.en: However, the anchor person on your local news station, if they were attractive, was pretty fine to share a toothbrush with.
sentences.zh: 然而，如果你当地新闻台的主播长得很有魅力，共用牙刷似乎也没什么大不了的。

sentences.en: And people in your direct family or your best friends were also okay to share a toothbrush with.
sentences.zh: 而直系亲属或最好的朋友，共用牙刷也是可以接受的。

sentences.en: And so this speaks to two things.
sentences.zh: 这说明了两点。

sentences.en: One, familiarity and emotional connection.
sentences.zh: 第一，熟悉感和情感联系。

sentences.en: So people in your family or your best friends, you feel positively towards them, you're very familiar with them,
sentences.zh: 对于家人或挚友，你对他们抱有积极的态度，非常熟悉他们，

sentences.en: and therefore you sort of feel safe around their saliva.
sentences.zh: 因此你觉得接触他们的唾液是安全的。

sentences.en: The good-looking person on the television, beauty equals health equals okay.
sentences.zh: 电视上好看的人，美貌等于健康，等于没问题。

sentences.en: But the person that you dislike or the person who's a stranger is a lot likely to be either more contaminating or because you don't like them,
sentences.zh: 但你讨厌的人或陌生人，更有可能被视为具有污染性，或者仅仅因为你不喜欢他们，

sentences.en: purely because you don't like them.
sentences.zh: 纯粹是因为你不喜欢他们。

sentences.en: They could be good-looking and you could know they're very healthy.
sentences.zh: 他们可能长得好看，你也可能知道他们很健康。

sentences.en: But if you don't like them, then you don't want anything about them coming into you, as in their toothbrush.
sentences.zh: 但如果你不喜欢他们，你就不会想让他们身上的任何东西进入你的身体，比如他们的牙刷。

sentences.en: Context is key when it comes to disguSt.
sentences.zh: 谈到厌恶感，背景至关重要。

sentences.en: In October 1972, a plane crashed in an isolated region of the Andes mountain range.
sentences.zh: 1972年10月，一架飞机在安第斯山脉的一个偏远地区坠毁。

sentences.en: There were 45 people on board, most of them rugby players, traveling to Chile for a competition.
sentences.zh: 机上有45人，大多数是橄榄球运动员，正前往智利参加比赛。

sentences.en: Many passengers died upon impact.
sentences.zh: 许多乘客在撞击时就丧生了。

sentences.en: More died in the coming days because of the freezing cold and dwindling food supply.
sentences.zh: 由于严寒和食物短缺，随后几天又有更多人死亡。

sentences.en: In the end, 16 people had to survive more than two months in the mountains,
sentences.zh: 最终，16人不得不在山中生存了两个多月，

sentences.en: and their story has inspired movies, books, and documentaries like this one from the History Channel.
sentences.zh: 他们的故事启发了电影、书籍和纪录片，比如历史频道的这一部。

sentences.en: I said, Nando, there isn't anything left in the storage compartments where we kept the chocolates and the can of sardines that we had.
sentences.zh: 我说：“南多，我们存放巧克力和沙丁鱼罐头的储物格里什么都不剩了。”

sentences.en: And Nando looked me in the eye and said,
sentences.zh: 南多看着我的眼睛说：

sentences.en: Carlitos, I want to eat the pilot.
sentences.zh: “卡利托斯，我想吃掉飞行员。”

sentences.en: The people that had this idea and wanted to convince the other members that this was the only way they were going to survive did two things.
sentences.zh: 那些提出这个想法并试图说服其他成员这是他们唯一生存之道的人，做了两件事。

sentences.en: One, they told the people to think of this as what you're doing is eating just meat.
sentences.zh: 第一，他们告诉大家，把这看作只是在吃肉。

sentences.en: So don't think about this as a person.
sentences.zh: 所以不要把它想成是一个人。

sentences.en: Kind of connected to we don't think about eating cows and pigs so much as we think of eating pork and beef.
sentences.zh: 这有点像我们吃猪肉和牛肉时，并不会过多地去想我们是在吃猪和牛。

sentences.en: So this is just meat.
sentences.zh: 所以这只是肉。

sentences.en: And the second thing is that they tried to justify this in another kind of a moral way by saying that the death of their compatriots would have been sort of a complete waste
sentences.zh: 第二件事是，他们试图从另一种道德层面来证明这一点，称如果同伴的死不能以这种方式来帮助他们生存，

sentences.en: if it couldn't be used in this way to potentially aid in their survival.
sentences.zh: 那将是一种彻底的浪费。

sentences.en: And so reluctantly at first, but then everybody joined in, ate the dead remains of the people that were around them.
sentences.zh: 于是，起初虽然勉强，但后来每个人都加入了，吃掉了周围死者的遗体。

sentences.en: And another thing they did.
sentences.zh: 他们还做了另一件事。

sentences.en: So the fact that this is about cannibalism and that the people willingly resorted to this
sentences.zh: 关于食人行为以及人们自愿采取这种做法的事实，

sentences.en: is something which has really caught our imagination because it really leads to this question of what would you do in that circumstance?
sentences.zh: 确实引起了我们的想象，因为它引出了一个问题：在这种情况下你会怎么做？

sentences.en: Would you also, you know, traverse the line into this worst taboo?
sentences.zh: 你也会跨越这条底线，触碰这个最严重的禁忌吗？

sentences.en: One of the things that I find interesting is that when I personally think about their behavior,
sentences.zh: 我发现有趣的一点是，当我个人思考他们的行为时，

sentences.en: I don't necessarily feel disgusted by what they did in the same way that if you told me that someone was munching on their neighbor's arm.
sentences.zh: 我并不像听到有人在啃邻居的手臂那样，对他们的所作所为感到同样的恶心。

sentences.en: You know, there's something about essentially having your hand forced by circumstances.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你的处境迫使你不得不这样做时，情况是不一样的。

sentences.en: You're acting in a way that is the only way you can possibly survive.
sentences.zh: 你的行为是你能生存下去的唯一方式。

sentences.en: That changes the way I think about whether this is disgusting.
sentences.zh: 这改变了我对这种行为是否恶心的看法。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's only really disgusting when it's a willful, unnecessary behavior.
sentences.zh: 只有当它是蓄意的、不必要的行为时，才真正令人恶心。

sentences.en: So like you said, you know, you kill your neighbor and then decide to eat them.
sentences.zh: 就像你说的，如果你杀了邻居然后决定吃掉他们。

sentences.en: But someone who is forced into this situation and the only way that they can survive is by resorting to an opportunistic situation.
sentences.zh: 但对于一个被迫陷入这种境地，且只能通过这种机会主义方式生存的人来说，

sentences.en: The person's already dead.
sentences.zh: 那个人已经死了。

sentences.en: That's a lot different.
sentences.zh: 这大不相同。

sentences.en: But the act itself, eating someone who's dead, eating another dead human being is the same.
sentences.zh: 但行为本身，吃掉一个死人，吃掉另一个人，是一样的。

sentences.en: And again, this is how our mind changes the behavior from being okay to something completely abhorrent.
sentences.zh: 同样，这就是我们的思想如何将行为从“可以接受”转变为“极其令人厌恶”的过程。

sentences.en: Rachel, you describe a case that took place in the 1990s.
sentences.zh: 瑞秋，你描述了一个发生在20世纪90年代的案件。

sentences.en: A man was stomped to death after propositioning another man.
sentences.zh: 一名男子在向另一名男子求爱后被踩踏致死。

sentences.en: And when the case was taken to court, the defendant successfully used something known as the gay panic defense.
sentences.zh: 当案件提交法庭时，被告成功使用了所谓的“同性恋恐慌辩护”。

sentences.en: You say this idea is rooted in a misconception about disgust?
sentences.zh: 你说这个想法植根于对厌恶感的误解？

sentences.en: So this idea that in this sense, using the gay panic defense.
sentences.zh: 所以，在这个意义上使用“同性恋恐慌辩护”的想法，

sentences.en: So in this case, someone was able to convince a jury that the idea of this man making a homosexual advance to him was so repugnant that being, you know,
sentences.zh: 在这个案件中，有人成功说服陪审团，认为这个男人向他提出同性恋请求的想法是如此令人反感，以至于，你知道，

sentences.en: motivated to kill this person was somehow justified.
sentences.zh: 出于这种动机去杀人，在某种程度上是合理的。

sentences.en: And like you said, it actually was successful in the trial.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，它在审判中确实成功了。

sentences.en: Now, the concept that I think, so this is sort of,
sentences.zh: 现在，我认为这个概念，这有点像，

sentences.en: this is moralizing and this is getting people to become less judgmental towards the act of murder because of the fact that they felt a kind of a sympathy towards the feeling of aversion that this person must have had.
sentences.zh: 这是在进行道德说教，让人们对谋杀行为减少评判，因为他们对这个人当时感到的厌恶情绪产生了一种同情。

sentences.en: And therefore, this sort of outburst of rage is somehow justified.
sentences.zh: 因此，这种愤怒的爆发在某种程度上是合理的。

sentences.en: The thing that's different about this, and I think this is an interesting point about disgust and what makes it different from anger, which I think it's often confused with,
sentences.zh: 这件事的不同之处在于——我认为这是关于厌恶感的一个有趣点，它与经常被混淆的愤怒不同——

sentences.en: is that disgust is about recoiling from, moving away from, avoiding the stimulus that's making you disgusted.
sentences.zh: 厌恶感是关于退缩、远离、避开让你感到恶心的刺激物。

sentences.en: And if someone were truly disgusted by somebody else,
sentences.zh: 如果一个人真的对另一个人感到恶心，

sentences.en: they would not want to get all over them and beat them to death and get their blood and everything else all over them because that would be even more disgusting if you're already disgusted.
sentences.zh: 他们是不会想去接触对方并把对方打死，弄得满身是血的，因为如果你已经感到恶心了，那会更恶心。

sentences.en: Instead, if I'm really angry, if I'm enraged by something, then I attack, then I approach, then I can, you know,
sentences.zh: 相反，如果我真的很愤怒，如果我被某事激怒了，那么我会攻击，我会靠近，那么我可以，你知道，

sentences.en: demolish you and get all covered in you and it doesn't matter because I'm just in a rage.
sentences.zh: 摧毁你，弄得满身都是你，这没关系，因为我正处于愤怒之中。

sentences.en: So really, the idea about this being disgust is wrong.
sentences.zh: 所以，认为这是厌恶感的想法是错误的。

sentences.en: And what it was is this person was affronted, you know, somehow morally, personally, whatever the case might be,
sentences.zh: 事实是这个人受到了冒犯，你知道，在道德上、个人层面上，无论情况如何，

sentences.en: and incited into such a rage that then he wanted to murder this person.
sentences.zh: 并被激怒到想要谋杀这个人。

sentences.en: So the idea of using disgust in this way is actually flawed because the person is not disgusted.
sentences.zh: 所以以这种方式使用“厌恶”这个概念实际上是有缺陷的，因为那个人并不觉得恶心。

sentences.en: They're just enraged.
sentences.zh: 他们只是被激怒了。

sentences.en: So that example of homophobia, Rachel, makes me think about an idea.
sentences.zh: 瑞秋，那个关于恐同的例子让我想到了一个观点。

sentences.en: In almost every society you go to, you see patterns of disgust that are modeled on social hierarchies.
sentences.zh: 在几乎每一个社会中，你都能看到以社会等级为蓝本的厌恶模式。

sentences.en: In many countries,
sentences.zh: 在许多国家，

sentences.en: you have the rich who are disgusted by the poor or upper castes who are disgusted by lower castes or people who are native citizens being disgusted by foreigners.
sentences.zh: 富人厌恶穷人，高种姓厌恶低种姓，或者本地公民厌恶外国人。

sentences.en: What do you think explains this?
sentences.zh: 你认为这该如何解释？

sentences.en: It has to do with something more insidious, and that's related to our feelings about our social environment and the people that are in it.
sentences.zh: 这与更阴险的东西有关，与我们对社会环境及其中人们的感受有关。

sentences.en: And the idea that foreigners and strangers and so forth are threats to our social normal order,
sentences.zh: 这种观点认为，外国人、陌生人等等是对我们社会正常秩序的威胁，

sentences.en: and that that then becomes somehow connected to our ideas about contamination and protecting us somehow.
sentences.zh: 这随后在某种程度上与我们关于污染和保护自身的想法联系在了一起。

sentences.en: And the idea is that this somehow justifies and rationalizes racial prejudices and other kinds of prejudices, because if we stay away from the unfamiliar and the foreign,
sentences.zh: 其核心在于，这在某种程度上证明并合理化了种族偏见和其他偏见，因为如果我们远离不熟悉和外国的事物，

sentences.en: because we don't know what those immigrants, you know, they could be diseased.
sentences.zh: 因为我们不知道那些移民，你知道，他们可能带有疾病。

sentences.en: And in fact, disease was often used as a way of anti-immigrant propaganda.
sentences.zh: 事实上，疾病经常被用作反移民宣传的一种手段。

sentences.en: This somehow justifies negative attitudes towards them when there's no relationship between their ability to actually make us sick or not.
sentences.zh: 这在某种程度上证明了对他们的负面态度是合理的，尽管他们是否有能力让我们生病之间并没有任何关系。

sentences.en: In much of our life, disgust feels instinctive.
sentences.zh: 在我们的大部分生活中，厌恶感似乎是本能的。

sentences.en: When we see a cockroach on a kitchen counter or smell rotten food in the trash can, our revulsion feels hardwired.
sentences.zh: 当我们看到厨房台面上的蟑螂或闻到垃圾桶里腐烂食物的味道时，我们的反感似乎是与生俱来的。

sentences.en: But Rachel says it's not.
sentences.zh: 但瑞秋说并非如此。

sentences.en: Our sense of disgust is learned.
sentences.zh: 我们的厌恶感是后天习得的。

sentences.en: The things that disgust us not only reveal a lot about our culture, they reveal a great deal about our minds.
sentences.zh: 让我们感到恶心的事物不仅揭示了我们的文化，也揭示了我们的思想。

sentences.en: She remembers an instructive episode from her own childhood.
sentences.zh: 她记得童年时期的一个启发性片段。

sentences.en: As we were driving in the car and it was a beautiful, sunny summer day and the windows were rolled down and there were, you know,
sentences.zh: 当时我们正开车，那是一个阳光明媚的夏日，车窗摇了下来，你知道，

sentences.en: we were going by fields and everything was very pretty.
sentences.zh: 我们经过田野，一切都很美。

sentences.en: My mother from the front seat said, oh, I love that smell.
sentences.zh: 我母亲从前座说：“哦，我喜欢那个味道。”

sentences.en: And so as I was smelling the same thing and all kinds of nice things were in my visual scene and my mother, who I love, said, I love that smell.
sentences.zh: 当我闻到同样的味道，眼前看到各种美好的事物，而我爱的母亲说她喜欢那个味道时，

sentences.en: I thought, OK, this is a great smell.
sentences.zh: 我想，好吧，这是一种很棒的味道。

sentences.en: And I then learned a few years later that saying that in response to that smell was a very big mistake.
sentences.zh: 几年后我才知道，针对那种味道说出那句话是一个非常大的错误。

sentences.en: So the smell turned out to be skunk.
sentences.zh: 原来那是臭鼬的味道。

sentences.en: So when I said I love that smell on the playground with all a bunch of little kids around me and they went, ew, disgusting, that skunk.
sentences.zh: 所以当我在操场上，周围有一群小孩时，我说我喜欢那个味道，他们就说：“咦，真恶心，那是臭鼬。”

sentences.en: Oh, you're so gross and so forth and ran away from me.
sentences.zh: “哦，你真恶心”之类的，然后从我身边跑开了。

sentences.en: Again, so I become now the skunk because they all ran away from me.
sentences.zh: 同样，我现在变成了那只臭鼬，因为他们都从我身边跑开了。

sentences.en: I realized that was not the socially appropriate thing to say.
sentences.zh: 我意识到那不是社交场合中合适的说法。

sentences.en: And so I kept that to myself for quite a while.
sentences.zh: 所以我把那句话藏在心里很久。

sentences.en: But it turns out I'm not alone.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明我并不孤单。

sentences.en: There are actually people who like the smell of skunk.
sentences.zh: 确实有人喜欢臭鼬的味道。

sentences.en: And that also leads into something interesting about our sense of smell.
sentences.zh: 这也引出了关于我们嗅觉的一些有趣的事情。

sentences.en: In fact, we don't all smell skunk in the same way.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们闻到的臭鼬味并不完全相同。

sentences.en: So both our minds and the way our noses, in fact, react to the chemical that makes up skunk is different.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们的思想以及我们的鼻子对构成臭鼬味的化学物质的反应确实是不同的。

sentences.en: So unless you have an identical twin, your receptors in your nose are actually only yours and nobody else shares them, even though there's a lot of overlap.
sentences.zh: 除非你有同卵双胞胎，否则你鼻子里的受体实际上只属于你，没有人与你共享，尽管它们有很多重叠之处。

sentences.en: So I buy the idea that we're all not smelling the same thing when we smell skunk, that the receptors in our noses and the way our brains work, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以我相信我们闻臭鼬味时闻到的东西并不一样，我们鼻子里的受体和大脑的工作方式，你知道，

sentences.en: we might be smelling different things.
sentences.zh: 我们闻到的可能是不同的东西。

sentences.en: But it's also what I find really fascinating about the story is that there is so much about disgust that is actually learned.
sentences.zh: 但这个故事真正让我着迷的是，关于厌恶感，有太多东西实际上是后天习得的。

sentences.en: You heard your mother.
sentences.zh: 你听到了你母亲的话。

sentences.en: You have an association between your mother and the beautiful scenery around you.
sentences.zh: 你把你母亲和你周围美丽的风景联系在了一起。

sentences.en: And you learn in some ways whether something that's a strong smell is a positive smell or a negative smell.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，你学会了某种强烈的气味是积极的还是消极的。

sentences.en: And in many ways, this runs counter to the way most of us, I think, think about disguSt.
sentences.zh: 在很多方面，我认为这与我们大多数人对厌恶感的看法背道而驰。

sentences.en: We think of it as being this innate drive that if I find something disgusting, you're going to smell it and you're going to find it disgusting as well.
sentences.zh: 我们认为这是一种天生的驱动力，如果我发现某样东西恶心，你闻到它也会觉得恶心。

sentences.en: So I think that brings up a great way to think about the idea of disguSt.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这提供了一个思考厌恶感的好方法。

sentences.en: And it is that it is the instinct that has to be learned.
sentences.zh: 那就是，这是一种必须习得的本能。

sentences.en: So once we learn what something disgusting is, we then feel disgusted by it.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦我们学会了什么是恶心的，我们就会对它感到厌恶。

sentences.en: Like, for instance, bodily products and toilet training and, you know, poop and so forth.
sentences.zh: 比如，身体排泄物、如厕训练，你知道，粪便等等。

sentences.en: We don't have a question about whether or not it's disgusting, especially if it's from somebody else where also is where meaning and context come into play.
sentences.zh: 我们不会质疑它是否恶心，特别是如果它来自别人，这也是意义和背景发挥作用的地方。

sentences.en: But we did not think it was disgusting from the get go.
sentences.zh: 但我们一开始并不觉得它恶心。

sentences.en: So that is to say we were not hardwired or born thinking that poop was gross.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，我们并不是天生就觉得粪便很恶心。

sentences.en: In fact, many infants both like to play with poop.
sentences.zh: 事实上，许多婴儿喜欢玩粪便。

sentences.en: They like the smell of poop.
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢粪便的味道。

sentences.en: They don't have any reactions to things, for instance, that adults in the same community think of as positive or negative.
sentences.zh: 对于同一社区的成年人认为是积极或消极的事物，他们没有任何反应。

sentences.en: In fact, a great demonstration I like to do is showing these facial expressions of babies getting either the smell of sort of sweaty socks and vomit versus the smell of vanilla.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我喜欢做一个很棒的演示，展示婴儿闻到汗袜子和呕吐物的味道，以及闻到香草味时的面部表情。

sentences.en: And some babies' faces to the sweaty socks and vomit are making big smiley faces.
sentences.zh: 有些婴儿对汗袜子和呕吐物的味道会做出大大的笑脸。

sentences.en: And others to the face to the smell of vanilla are making what we would call disgust faces.
sentences.zh: 而另一些婴儿对香草味则会做出我们所谓的厌恶表情。

sentences.en: So, you know, there's nothing hardwired about the reaction either to smells or to things that are disgusting.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，无论是对气味还是对令人恶心的事物的反应，都没有什么是天生的。

sentences.en: But once we learn what the meaning is, we then stick to it, except for when the context can make it very confusing or the context changes the way we perceive something.
sentences.zh: 但一旦我们理解了它的含义，我们就会坚持这种看法，除非背景会让它变得非常令人困惑，或者背景改变了我们感知某事物的方式。

sentences.en: I love this idea that in many ways our notions of disgust are constructed.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个观点，即在很多方面，我们的厌恶感概念是被构建出来的。

sentences.en: I understand that Americans like wintergreen-flavored chewing gum, but people in Britain, not so much.
sentences.zh: 我知道美国人喜欢冬青味的口香糖，但英国人不太喜欢。

sentences.en: So in the U.K., wintergreen mint is used exclusively in toilet cleaning products and in some medicinal balms, like things you would rub on your skin if you're in pain.
sentences.zh: 在英国，冬青薄荷味仅用于厕所清洁产品和一些药用软膏，比如你感到疼痛时涂在皮肤上的东西。

sentences.en: And so they're connected.
sentences.zh: 所以它们是联系在一起的。

sentences.en: The smell is connected to either being in pain or cleaning the toilet.
sentences.zh: 这种气味要么与痛苦有关，要么与打扫厕所联系在一起。

sentences.en: So not good.
sentences.zh: 所以感觉并不好。

sentences.en: In the U.S., however, the scent is used in candies and in guMs.
sentences.zh: 然而在美国，这种香味被用于糖果和口香糖中。

sentences.en: It's connected to the taste of sweet, and sweet actually is innately positive.
sentences.zh: 它与甜味联系在一起，而甜味本质上是令人愉悦的。

sentences.en: So tasting sweet plus smelling something, that's going to be good.
sentences.zh: 所以品尝甜味再加上闻到某种气味，那感觉会很不错。

sentences.en: And we don't have any connection to cleaning the bathroom or being in pain when we smell this odor.
sentences.zh: 而且当我们闻到这种气味时，并没有把它与打扫厕所或痛苦联系起来。

sentences.en: And so as a function of the connections that we have learned to it and what the meaning is, this odor, which in and of itself is totally, you know, agnostic,
sentences.zh: 因此，基于我们对它所建立的联想及其含义，这种气味本身其实是完全中性的，你知道的，

sentences.en: it doesn't have meaning one way or the other, becomes good or becomes bad as a function of that.
sentences.zh: 它本身并没有好坏之分，而是根据这些联想变得好或坏。

sentences.en: So the British and the Americans are divided on the subject of wintergreen.
sentences.zh: 所以英国人和美国人在冬青味的问题上存在分歧。

sentences.en: But I'm absolutely sure they'd come together when it comes to eating bugs.
sentences.zh: 但我敢肯定，在吃虫子这件事上，他们会达成一致。

sentences.en: It ain't happening.
sentences.zh: 这绝对不可能。

sentences.en: My heart's pounding.
sentences.zh: 我的心跳得好快。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: They look like crickets.
sentences.zh: 它们看起来像蟋蟀。

sentences.en: There's no sugarcoating.
sentences.zh: 没什么好掩饰的。

sentences.en: I'm about to throw up if I stay here.
sentences.zh: 如果我再待在这里，我就要吐了。

sentences.en: Oh, I don't want to do it.
sentences.zh: 噢，我不想吃。

sentences.en: Those are reactions from a couple of our NPR co-workers when we presented them with a plate of dried crickets and asked them to take a bite.
sentences.zh: 这些是我们几位NPR同事的反应，当时我们给他们端上一盘干蟋蟀，并请他们尝一口。

sentences.en: Can I go fill up my water bottle?
sentences.zh: 我可以去装满我的水瓶吗？

sentences.en: Can I have a chaser?
sentences.zh: 能给我点喝的压压惊吗？

sentences.en: I'm cool with bugs as long as they're outside.
sentences.zh: 只要虫子在外面，我完全没问题。

sentences.en: I'm not sure how cool I am with them being in my mouth.
sentences.zh: 但我不太确定把它们放进嘴里我还能不能接受。

sentences.en: It's disgusting.
sentences.zh: 太恶心了。

sentences.en: It's insects.
sentences.zh: 这是昆虫啊。

sentences.en: Look at it.
sentences.zh: 看看它。

sentences.en: There's exoskeletons everywhere and pieces of legs.
sentences.zh: 到处都是外骨骼和腿的碎片。

sentences.en: This is gross.
sentences.zh: 这太反胃了。

sentences.en: People eat this?
sentences.zh: 真的有人吃这个？

sentences.en: There's a couple of things which disgust us about bugs.
sentences.zh: 关于虫子，有几点让我们感到恶心。

sentences.en: One of them is that we don't consider them to be food.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是我们根本不认为它们是食物。

sentences.en: Now, there are cultures, especially in Southeast Asia, that do consider all kinds of bugs as food.
sentences.zh: 当然，有些文化，特别是在东南亚，确实把各种虫子视为食物。

sentences.en: And if you were to go to Thailand,
sentences.zh: 如果你去泰国的话，

sentences.en: you'd see Madagascar hissing cockroaches on display in the market where people are actually buying them to eat them up for meals and prepare them in all kinds of ways,
sentences.zh: 你会看到市场上摆着马达加斯加发声蟑螂，人们真的会买来当作餐点，并用各种方式烹饪它们，

sentences.en: which apparently, although I don't know personally, can be quite delicious.
sentences.zh: 虽然我没亲口尝过，但据说味道相当不错。

sentences.en: But the idea of what food is is a really interesting concept because this, again, speaks to how disgust is learned.
sentences.zh: 但关于什么是食物的想法是一个非常有趣的概念，因为这再次说明了厌恶感是如何习得的。

sentences.en: And when we decide that something is edible, then it's okay to eat.
sentences.zh: 当我们认定某样东西可以食用时，那吃它就没问题。

sentences.en: And other cultures think differently about that.
sentences.zh: 而其他文化对此有不同的看法。

sentences.en: The other thing about bugs is that they move in a way that seems to be related to one of the aspects of disgust underlying why we don't like them.
sentences.zh: 关于虫子的另一件事是，它们的移动方式似乎与我们厌恶它们背后的某些方面有关。

sentences.en: And this is actually somewhat connected to bodily fluids.
sentences.zh: 这实际上与体液有些关联。

sentences.en: So bugs move in a kind of a jerky or slithery or slimy kind of way.
sentences.zh: 虫子的移动方式通常是抽动、滑行或黏糊糊的。

sentences.en: And those kinds of things actually have a similarity to body products that we are also disgusted by.
sentences.zh: 而这些特征实际上与我们同样感到厌恶的身体排泄物有相似之处。

sentences.en: So being disgusted by slugs, for instance, is to do with the fact that slugs are similar visually to feces.
sentences.zh: 例如，对蛞蝓感到厌恶，是因为蛞蝓在视觉上与粪便相似。

sentences.en: So there is this kind of continuum about our association between what bugs are and what bodily fluids are that we're disgusted by.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们对虫子的认知与我们厌恶的体液之间存在一种连续性。

sentences.en: So there's a variety of reasons why bugs are disgusting.
sentences.zh: 因此，虫子令人厌恶的原因有很多。

sentences.en: One of the things in your book that caught my eye was even in the same country, in different periods of time,
sentences.zh: 你书中的一点引起了我的注意，即使在同一个国家，在不同的时期，

sentences.en: our attitudes about what's disgusting have changed or can change enormously.
sentences.zh: 我们对什么是令人厌恶的态度已经改变，或者说可能会发生巨大的改变。

sentences.en: I understand that a few centuries ago, lobster was not quite seen the way that it was in Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 我听说几个世纪前，龙虾在马萨诸塞州的待遇和现在完全不同。

sentences.en: No, lobster was actually considered vermin of the sea and only suitable for slaves.
sentences.zh: 没错，龙虾当时实际上被认为是海里的害虫，只适合奴隶吃。

sentences.en: And in fact, there was a slave uprising against the idea that it was it was completely cruel and unusual punishment to give people lobster to eat more than three times a week.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当时还发生过奴隶起义，因为人们认为每周给他们吃三次龙虾是极其残忍和不寻常的惩罚。

sentences.en: And today we might say, oh, how lucky to be able to afford to have lobster three times a week.
sentences.zh: 而今天我们可能会说，能吃得起每周三次龙虾是多么幸运啊。

sentences.en: So it's conceivable then maybe in a few decades or maybe in a couple of centuries from now, we will think of eating cockroaches and crickets very differently than we do today.
sentences.zh: 所以可以想象，也许几十年或几个世纪后，我们对吃蟑螂和蟋蟀的看法会与今天大不相同。

sentences.en: In fact, there are some people who would argue that insects are a very efficient source of protein and they are plentiful.
sentences.zh: 事实上，有些人认为昆虫是一种非常高效的蛋白质来源，而且数量充足。

sentences.en: And in some ways, consuming insects might actually be good for the environment in all kinds of different ways.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，食用昆虫实际上可能对环境有各种各样的好处。

sentences.en: I'm personally a vegetarian, so I don't know if I'll ever subscribe to eating crickets and cockroaches.
sentences.zh: 我个人是素食主义者，所以我不知道自己是否会接受吃蟋蟀和蟑螂。

sentences.en: But presumably, our attitudes towards eating insects could change.
sentences.zh: 但可以推测，我们对食用昆虫的态度可能会改变。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对会。

sentences.en: So the idea also, one of the things that made lobster disgusting and unappealing is that it was slave food.
sentences.zh: 所以，让龙虾变得恶心且不受欢迎的原因之一，是它曾是奴隶的食物。

sentences.en: It was prisoner food.
sentences.zh: 那是囚犯的食物。

sentences.en: So these people, these are bad people in the kind of the hierarchy of humans.
sentences.zh: 所以这些人，在人类等级制度中，他们被视为低等的人。

sentences.en: And therefore, it's OK for them to eat things that are possibly that we would consider disgusting, but not OK for me, you know,
sentences.zh: 因此，他们吃我们认为恶心的东西是可以接受的，但对我来说不行，你知道，

sentences.en: the elevated person or whatever I think of myself as being.
sentences.zh: 那种自认为高人一等的人。

sentences.en: And right now, the way we think about insects is similar to that.
sentences.zh: 而现在，我们看待昆虫的方式也与之类似。

sentences.en: So people who are not like us, people who have to resort to the last measures possible for survival, they're going to debase themselves to eat insects.
sentences.zh: 所以那些与我们不同的人，那些为了生存不得不采取最后手段的人，他们会为了吃昆虫而自贬身价。

sentences.en: But if we think about it entirely differently,
sentences.zh: 但如果我们换个角度思考，

sentences.en: so if we remoralize the story and instead make eating insects about saving the planet and make it a virtuous thing to do rather than somehow a debase thing to do or a last resort thing to do,
sentences.zh: 如果我们重新赋予这个故事道德意义，把吃昆虫变成拯救地球的行为，让它成为一种美德，而不是一种自贬或最后的手段，

sentences.en: we could, in fact, make it a very positive thing.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上可以把它变成一件非常积极的事情。

sentences.en: While some of our co-workers shrank at first when they held the cricket in their hand.
sentences.zh: 虽然我们的一些同事起初在手里拿着蟋蟀时退缩了。

sentences.en: The more you look in his eyes, the less you want to eat it.
sentences.zh: 你盯着它的眼睛看越久，就越不想吃它。

sentences.en: The looks of fear and disgust faded after the first crunch.
sentences.zh: 在第一口咬下去之后，恐惧和厌恶的神情就消失了。

sentences.en: Cheers.
sentences.zh: 干杯。

sentences.en: Cheers.
sentences.zh: 干杯。

sentences.en: It's just like chips, kind of.
sentences.zh: 吃起来就像薯片一样，某种程度上。

sentences.en: It's good.
sentences.zh: 味道不错。

sentences.en: It's a little earthy.
sentences.zh: 有一点泥土味。

sentences.en: It's like sunflower seed or something.
sentences.zh: 就像葵花籽之类的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's like, can I get like a basket of these, like before my meal comes?
sentences.zh: 是啊，我在想，能在上正餐前给我来一篮这个吗？

sentences.en: Along with the whole crickets, we also provided samples of delectable protein bars made of cricket flour.
sentences.zh: 除了整只蟋蟀，我们还提供了用蟋蟀粉制成的美味蛋白棒样品。

sentences.en: I chose peanut butter and chocolate.
sentences.zh: 我选了花生酱和巧克力口味的。

sentences.en: If you didn't tell people this was cricket, they wouldn't know.
sentences.zh: 如果你不告诉别人这是蟋蟀做的，他们根本吃不出来。

sentences.en: It's good.
sentences.zh: 味道很好。

sentences.en: It's not like there's big chunks of cricket in it, so I like it.
sentences.zh: 里面又没有大块的蟋蟀，所以我很喜欢。

sentences.en: Not bad at all.
sentences.zh: 一点也不差。

sentences.en: I'm trying to not be so, like, American, you know, because everyone else eats crickets.
sentences.zh: 我正试着不要那么“美国化”，你知道，因为其他人都在吃蟋蟀。

sentences.en: It is a luxury to be able to be disgusted.
sentences.zh: 能够感到厌恶是一种奢侈。

sentences.en: From the very basic level that if you don't have anything else to eat other than someone who's dead beside you
sentences.zh: 从最基本的层面来说，如果你除了身边死人之外没有别的东西可吃，

sentences.en: or the cockroach on the floor, then you just do not get disgusted by that
sentences.zh: 或者地板上的蟑螂，那你根本就不会对这些感到厌恶，

sentences.en: because you have to do it in order to survive.
sentences.zh: 因为为了生存你必须这么做。

sentences.en: So it's a privilege to be able to say, no, I'd rather not have that dead person or that cockroach.
sentences.zh: 所以，能够说“不，我宁愿不吃那个死人或那只蟑螂”是一种特权。

sentences.en: I'd rather have that hamburger or the steak or that beautifully prepared dish of portobello mushrooMs.
sentences.zh: 我宁愿吃那个汉堡、牛排，或者那道精心烹制的波特菇料理。

sentences.en: So the ability to say that we are disgusted by something actually comes from the privilege
sentences.zh: 所以，能够说我们对某样东西感到厌恶，实际上源于一种特权，

sentences.en: and the luxury of having abundance and having enough to sustain us that we can make the decision
sentences.zh: 源于拥有充足资源和足够维持生存的奢侈，这样我们才能做出决定，

sentences.en: that we don't want this and we'd rather have that.
sentences.zh: 我们不想要这个，我们宁愿要那个。
